ai.description: *Cnemaspis indraneildasii* reaches 40 mm SVL. It is dark brown with a yellow-spotted vertebral stripe and orange-tipped tubercles. Distinctive features include a slender body and keeled ventral scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cnemaspis indraneildasii* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, bright yellow or orange patch on the throat, which is absent in other sympatric species.
ai.habitat: Cnemaspis indraneildasii inhabits the moist deciduous and evergreen forests of the southern Western Ghats, typically found on rock surfaces at elevations of 300–800 meters.
ai.behavior: *Cnemaspis indraneildasii* is primarily nocturnal, emerging from rock crevices at night to forage for small invertebrates on vertical surfaces.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis indraneildasii* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two spherical eggs. Breeding occurs throughout the year, with peak activity observed during the monsoon months.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cnemaspis indraneildasii* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala, India, typically found at elevations between 800 and 1,100 meters.
